body_text:
Cauchy--Riemann equations. Write $f(x+iy)=u(x,y)+iv(x,y)$. If $f$
is complex differentiable at $z_0=x_0+iy_0$ and the relevant real
partial derivatives exist, then at $(x_0,y_0)$ one has $u_x=v_y$
and $u_y=-v_x$. Conversely, if $u$ and $v$ have continuous first
partial derivatives on a neighborhood of $(x_0,y_0)$ and satisfy
these equations there, then $f$ is complex differentiable at
$z_0$.
